clue.text: Sign on closet for personal assistants

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the sign after the closet word

parts.note: closet as an adjective means secret, hidden
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A notice is pinned to a cupboard door telling staff where their assistants are.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretaries are office staff who assist an individual executive, the classic personal assistant role.

clue.text: One coming in to join one in army

indicators.note: coming in tells us the one enters the middle of the joining word

parts.note: to solder is to join metal pieces with molten alloy
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A recruit arrives to sign up alongside another member of the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a serving member of an army, so one person in it.

clue.text: Vegetable, primarily chewy and unpleasant

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word chewy

parts.note: hard, as in hard times, can mean unpleasant or harsh

explanation.surface: A complaint about some vegetable being mostly tough and nasty to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green garden plant eaten for its leaves and stalks.

clue.text: Blot out imperfect pieces, about fifty

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the numeral
imperfect suggests the letters of pieces are put into a faulty, rearranged order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cover up roughly fifty flawed items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imperfect' rearranges PIECES to ECIPSE, and 'about' puts that around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to obscure or overshadow it, cutting off its light.

clue.text: Football club's stadium, outside south London initially

indicators.note: outside means the stadium word goes around the letter for south

parts.note: an arena is a stadium or sports ground
S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of London

explanation.surface: Talk of a football club whose ground lies beyond south London.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'); 'outside' wraps ARENA around S to give ARSENA, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a well-known professional football club based in north London.

clue.text: I left lake with a kid far from relaxed

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Someone describes leaving a lakeside with a child and feeling tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease means feeling uncomfortable and anxious, the opposite of relaxed.

clue.text: German bread taken round end of festival

indicators.note: round means the word for taken encloses the next letter

parts.note: taken in the sense of stolen

indicators.note: end of asks for the last letter of festival

explanation.surface: A German loaf is carried around at the close of a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a German fruit loaf traditionally baked for Christmas.

clue.text: Antique found in manor-house in large bag

indicators.note: found in places the antique word inside the house word

parts.note: a hall is a large country house or manor
antique means old

explanation.surface: An antique is discovered stuffed in a big bag at a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travel bag that holds plenty of belongings.

clue.text: Hotel employees all drink in this, occasionally

indicators.note: in puts all and the drink inside the letters taken from this
occasionally asks for every other letter of the word this

parts.note: porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Hotel staff are pictured all drinking in some establishment now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' looks like a pointer to some bar, but it is the source of the outer letters: 'occasionally' keeps only its second and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hall porters are hotel staff who carry luggage and assist guests in the lobby.

clue.text: Part of proposal for developing English city

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some urban redevelopment proposal for an English city is being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Salford is a city in Greater Manchester in the north-west of England.

clue.text: Boring campanologists should get doubles

parts.note: dead can mean dull or boring, as in a dead party
campanologists are bell-ringers

explanation.surface: A dig at dull bell-ringers who should take double measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead ringers are people who look exactly alike, lookalikes or doubles.

clue.text: Estate landowner coming out of retreat with daughter

parts.note: a lair is a hiding place or den to retreat to
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A landowner emerges from a hideaway accompanied by his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner with an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Laird is the Scots term for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Harshly criticise a bank clerk heard getting cigar

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: heard says the clerk word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk at the counter

explanation.surface: A bank worker is slated and then handed a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech TELLER sounds like TELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin type of cigar.

clue.text: Love tucking into medley of kipper and something from the butcher's?

indicators.note: tucking into puts the zero inside the jumbled letters
a medley is a mixture, so the letters of kipper are jumbled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so O

explanation.surface: Someone happily eats mixed kippers alongside a butcher's purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley of' rearranges KIPPER to PRKPIE; 'tucking into' sets O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a meat pie sold by butchers, an example of their wares, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Three of a kind, two of a kind, and a type of flush

parts.note: a pair is two cards of the same rank
a royal flush is the top poker hand, so royal names one type

explanation.surface: A run through poker hands: three of a kind, a pair, and a flush.
explanation.walkthrough: Pair royal is an old card-game term (used in cribbage) for three cards of the same rank.
explanation.definitionFit: In cards a pair royal is a set of three matching cards, i.e. three of a kind.

clue.text: Loewe's partner impressing a pupil

indicators.note: impressing means pressing the a into the partner's name

parts.note: Alan Jay Lerner wrote musicals such as My Fair Lady with Frederick Loewe

explanation.surface: A songwriter's collaborator wins over a student.
explanation.walkthrough: Lerner and Loewe were the lyricist-composer team behind My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone being taught, a student or pupil.

clue.text: Recovered and exchanged a series of shots

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as a patient or market picks up
second meaning: ..., as tennis players hit the ball back and forth

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gunfight; the shots are tennis strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is both to regain strength and to keep a long exchange of strokes going in racket sports.

clue.text: Unsophisticated, born in humble terrace?

indicators.note: in puts the letter for born within the humble terrace words

parts.note: low can mean humble or lowly
a terrace is a row of houses

explanation.surface: Someone brought up in a modest row of houses is called unrefined.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowbrow means lacking intellectual or cultural refinement.

clue.text: Shrink departs — con hasn't succeeded

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: hasn't says the con word is lacking the letter for succeeded

parts.note: a con is a swindle
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A conman's scam has failed and he leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to grow gradually smaller, diminishing in size or amount.

clue.text: Mischievous troublemaker — girl men reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of girl men are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A troublesome girl's male companions have mended their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for unexplained mechanical faults.

clue.text: Kind of cotton cloth inside bulging hamper

indicators.note: inside says the answer sits within the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of bulging into the start of hamper

explanation.surface: Some cotton fabric is stuffed in an overfull picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a light cotton fabric usually woven in checks, as on picnic cloths.

clue.text: Theft? Criminal nearly caught breaking in

indicators.note: breaking in puts the letter for caught into the rearranged letters
criminal suggests the letters of nearly are crookedly rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A thief was almost arrested while breaking into a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges NEARLY to LARENY; 'breaking in' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for stealing personal property.

clue.text: Post-Victorian hostilities suppressed by press chief and I, unwisely

indicators.note: suppressed by places the war after, as if held down by, the editor

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
war means hostilities

indicators.note: unwisely suggests the letters of and I are thrown together carelessly

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor and I foolishly stifle fighting after the Victorian age.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edwardian era followed Queen Victoria's reign, covering Edward VII's rule from 1901.

clue.text: Strain representing church

parts.note: for can mean on behalf of, representing
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Tension felt by someone acting for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Force as a verb means to strain or push hard, as in forcing a lock.

clue.text: Oldest evergreen on street

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places the tree above the street

parts.note: a fir is an evergreen tree
ST is the address abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: The most ancient evergreen tree grows on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: First can mean earliest, so the oldest or original one of something.

clue.text: Special rest day, so wandered off

indicators.note: special suggests the letters of rest day are made into something different

explanation.surface: Someone took a particular day off and so drifted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Strayed means moved away from the proper place or path, roaming.

clue.text: Tackle difficulty leader of Democrats ignored

indicators.note: ignored means that letter is left out of the difficulty word

parts.note: hardness means difficulty

indicators.note: leader of asks for the first letter of Democrats

explanation.surface: A political party's leader is overlooked while the problem is addressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb but is the noun for gear, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Harness and tackle are both words for equipment, especially the gear worn by a horse.

clue.text: Comic, pocketing change, beginning to mimic daydreamer

indicators.note: pocketing means the comic word holds the other letters

parts.note: witty means amusing, comic
to alter is to change

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of mimic

explanation.surface: A comedian who takes money is about to start an impression of a dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is the fantasising hero of James Thurber's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A Walter Mitty is an ordinary person who indulges in heroic fantasies.
